 TOP NEWS
 Introducing Healthy Home: A New Interactive, Online Experience:
 The American Lung Association’s Healthy Home is a new interactive educational tool that guides users through a virtual home, room by room, to identify potential indoor air quality hazards and “hot sports.” Participants can explore one of three housing types: single-family homes, multi-unit housing, or manufactured homes. In addition, users have free access to personalized education and support from health experts through our Lung HelpLine and Lung Health Navigator program, as well as a customizable  Indoor Air Quality Action Plan  and other educational resources.
 Learn more at www.Lung.org/healthy-home.   Also, read our blog, “ 10 Simple Steps for Healthier Air at Home.” 
 November is Lung Cancer Awareness Month
 Help us raise awareness about lung cancer and support people impacted by the disease:
 Meet our Lung Force Heroes .
 Learn more about lung cancer screening .
 Ask Congress to support the Clinical Trial Modernization Act , to reduce barriers that prevent people from participating in clinical trials.
 Learn more at Lung.org/lcam .
 Open Enrollment is Underway for Marketplace and Medicare Healthcare Coverage
 Open enrollment is now underway for both Medicare and Affordable Care Act (ACA) Marketplace health coverage. Medicare Open Enrollment runs through December 7, while enrollment for Affordable Care Act Marketplace coverage is open through January 15, 2027. This is an important opportunity to review your healthcare options and make sure your coverage continues to meet your needs.
 Medicare Open Enrollment. Medicare beneficiaries can switch health plan and/or Part D prescription drug plan during the annual enrollment period. In 2027, annual out-of-pocket prescription drug costs are capped at $2,400. Individuals with higher medication expenses may also benefit from the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan, which allows costs to be spread throughout the year. More information is available at Lung.org/Medicare .
 ACA Marketplace Open Enrollment. Enrollment for affordable, comprehensive health coverage through the ACA Marketplace starts November 1 and continues through January 15 in most states. Individuals renewing coverage should verify that their personal information, payment details and plan selections are up to date. More information on Marketplace options is available at Lung.org/OpenEnrollment .
 Lung Association Continues to Invest in High-Impact Research
 The American Lung Association  recently announced an additional $21 million investment, which includes $11million in direct research funding, to support 120 promising research projects in 2026–2027. As President and CEO Harold Wimmer emphasized, “We are proud to continue to invest in high-quality research with the potential to improve lung health for everyone.” Meet the new class of scientists making a difference: Lung.org/research-team 
 YOUR HEALTH 
 Pulmonary Hypertension Awareness Month  
 Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare lung disease that can be difficult to diagnose, often delaying vital treatment. This month, take a few minutes to learn more about how to live well with PAH.
 Start with Pulmonary Hypertension Basics to learn about diagnosis, treatment and support options.
 Read Jenna's story to learn how she is navigating life with PAH.
 ADVOCACY
 FDA Approves Marketing for 24 New Flavored Nicotine Pouches, Putting Kids at Risk
 Last month, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized the marketing of 24 new nicotine pouch products. The authorizations were issued as part of FDA's nicotine pouch pilot program. The Lung Association voiced our strong disagreement with this decision. 
 EPA Proposed Rollback of Methane Would Worsen Air Pollution and Health
 The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) recently proposed a rollback of the 2024 methane pollution limits designed to limit hazardous emissions from the oil and gas industry. The proposal would weaken critical methane protections, increase air pollution and harm health, particularly for communities near oil and gas sites. “If finalized, this proposal would help polluting industries avoid cleanup and harm the communities who bear the brunt of dirtier air and a warming planet," said Lung Association President & CEO Harold Wimmer in a statement . 
 Act Now: Join the Lung Association in urging EPA to uphold the 2024 Methane Rule. 
 EACH BREATH BLOG
 How an Unexpected Lung Cancer Diagnosis Led to a Radon Awareness Mission
 Cary, who lived a healthy lifestyle, was shocked when she received a stage 4  lung cancer diagnosis. While chemotherapy and a targeted therapy gave her hope and precious time, she was determined to understand what had caused her disease. She soon learned that environmental exposures, including  radon —the second leading cause of lung cancer—may have been a contributing factor, and testing revealed high levels of radon in her home. Today, Cary speaks to community organizations and the media, encouraging people to have their homes tested.  Read Cary’s story .
